title: Operators & Boolean Logic
summary: Calculate values, compare data, combine conditions, and recognize Python’s main operator families.
definition: Python includes arithmetic, comparison, assignment, logical, identity, membership, and bitwise operators. Choose the category that matches the task.
codeExample:
# Arithmetic
print(7 + 3, 7 - 3, 7 * 3)
print(7 / 2, 7 // 2, 7 % 2, 2 ** 3)

# Comparison
print(5 == 5, 5 != 3, 3 < 5, 5 > 3, 5 <= 5, 5 >= 3)

# Logical, membership, identity, and assignment
print(True and False, True or False, not True)
print("py" in "python", "z" not in "python")
value = None
print(value is None, value is not None)
score = 10
score += 2
print(score)

# Bitwise AND compares integer bits.
print(5 & 3)
howItWorks: Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, //, %, ** calculate values.
Comparison: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= return True or False.
Logic: and needs both conditions true; or needs at least one; not reverses truth.
Other families: = and += assign; in checks membership; is checks identity; bitwise operators work on integer bits.
fullExample:

quantity = 3
subtotal = price * quantity

print("Within budget:", subtotal <= 25 and quantity > 0)
print("Even total:", subtotal % 2 == 0)

# Assignment operators update a variable.
subtotal += 2
print("Updated:", subtotal)

# Membership checks whether a value is present.
codes = ["SAVE", "WELCOME"]
print("Has SAVE:", "SAVE" in codes)

# Identity is especially useful for checking None.
result = None
print("No result yet:", result is None)

# Bitwise operators work on the binary bits of integers.
print("5 & 3:", 5 & 3)
print("5 | 3:", 5 | 3)
print("5 ^ 3:", 5 ^ 3)
print("5 << 1:", 5 << 1)
print("5 >> 1:", 5 >> 1)
print("~5:", ~5)

while: Repeats while its condition is true; update the condition’s state so it can stop.

title: Performance & Practical Optimization
summary: Measure performance, recognize algorithmic costs, and optimize only where evidence supports it.
definition: Performance concerns execution time and resource use. Big-O notation describes how work grows as input size grows; data-structure choices can change that growth.

Verify: Compare results as well as time; timings vary across machines.
fullExample:
import time

values = list(range(200_000))
lookup_set = set(values)
target = 199_999

start = time.perf_counter()
found_in_list = target in values
list_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start

start = time.perf_counter()
found_in_set = target in lookup_set
set_seconds = time.perf_counter() - start

print("Same answer:", found_in_list == found_in_set)
print("List lookup seconds:", round(list_seconds, 6))
print("Set lookup seconds:", round(set_seconds, 6))
# Timings vary by machine; repeat measurements for meaningful comparisons.

title: Project 5: Production-Style Python Application
summary: Build your own small maintainable Python application from a specification, then test, document, and review it.
definition: The final project is an integration challenge. Choose a practical command-line application, design it yourself, and demonstrate that you can combine Python fundamentals with validation, persistence, testing, structure, and documentation.
howItWorks: 1. Requirements: write the features and success conditions before coding.
2. Plan: break the project into the smallest useful behaviors.
3. Guided build: implement one behavior, run it, and inspect the result.
4. Independent build: complete the next behavior without copying the full solution.
5. Debug & test: check normal, boundary, and invalid cases.
6. Review: improve one name, structure, or repeated section after tests pass.
practiceTask: Final project: choose a practical CLI app, write its requirements, build the core behavior yourself, test normal and invalid cases, document how to run it, and explain one design decision.
bio: A final integration project where you turn a clear specification into your own application instead of following a complete tutorial solution. The reference code remains available as a review example.
outcome: A small maintainable command-line application that you can explain, test, and run yourself.
